title: Incremental Memory Leak
summary: Given two integers memory1 and memory2, representing the available memory in bits on two memory sticks, a program consumes an increasing amount of memory every second.
statement: Given two integers memory1 and memory2, representing the available memory in bits on two memory sticks, a program consumes an increasing amount of memory every second. At the i^th second, i bits of memory are allocated to the stick with more available memory (or the first stick if both have the same available memory). If neither stick has at least i bits of available memory, the program crashes. Return an array [crashTime, memory1crash, memory2crash], indicating the time when the program crashes and the remaining memory on each stick.
constraints: At second i allocate i bits from the stick with more memory, choosing the first on ties.
Crash when neither stick has i bits; return [crash_second,remaining1,remaining2].
reference_solution:
def memory_leak_result(memory1, memory2):
 second=1
 while max(memory1,memory2)>=second:
  if memory1>=memory2:memory1-=second
  else:memory2-=second
  second+=1
 return [second,memory1,memory2]

hints: Simulate seconds because each allocation changes which stick is larger.
At each second subtract from the larger stick, choosing memory1 on equality.
Continue while the larger remaining capacity can satisfy the current second.
If the maximum capacity is below the request then neither stick can serve it; otherwise the stated choice and subtraction exactly reproduce that second.
